nodes.label: Bonzah policy PDF retrieval (Insillion passthrough, returned as base64)
Insillion PDF endpoint uses the generic /policy/data path with a URL-encoded token query param, not the /Bonzah/ prefix + in-auth-token header every other call uses
Tri-format PDF response tolerance (binary content-type, %PDF-prefixed text, JSON-wrapped base64)
Spendable Bonzah balance = the sub-user allocation, not the broker balance
Why a zero allocation must never fall back to the broker figure — $500 at broker / $0 allocated showed 'Accepting live policies' until a real customer's policy failed
needsAllocation flag — money sits at broker level but nothing is allocated to the issuing sub-account, and only the operator can move it inside Bonzah
Dual-endpoint balance read: /Bonzah/cdBalance (broker) plus /deposit (sub-user allocations), each failing independently
Bonzah low-balance alerting: reminder row + per-admin in-app notification + branded email
context.alerted latch stops re-notifying on every poll; recovery above the threshold resets the reminder to an info 'monitoring' state
Mode override swaps in the platform BONZAH_USERNAME/PASSWORD so a live tenant can still read its test balance
Threshold/alerting errors are swallowed so a notification failure never fails the balance request
Server-side Bonzah training-quiz grading (80% of active questions to pass)
Correct answers live only behind service_role — RLS plus an answer-omitting view keep correct_option_index off the client
Grading normally runs BEFORE the submission row exists (client carries the result into its insert); submissionId is the re-grade path that stamps quiz_* + training_completed_at
Bonzah partner approve/reject of an operator's onboarding submission
Partner gate — the caller must carry app_users.is_bonzah_partner = true, a role outside the tenant RBAC ladder
bonzah_mode is flipped to 'live' BEFORE verification so the creds authenticate against live, then rolled back to the previous mode if verification or persistence fails
Approval writes an 'approved' (partner) + 'activated' (system) event pair so the console timeline shows who acted and what the system then did
Approval persists the operator's Bonzah username/password onto tenants and sets integration_bonzah = true
Branded outcome emails are fire-and-forget (.catch(() => {})) — the review outcome is never blocked on mail delivery
Outcome notifications are inserted with user_id = null so every user of the tenant sees them, linked to /settings?tab=insurance
Brute-force discovery of the working Bonzah/Insillion PDF endpoint — 28 URL/method/body candidates probed in parallel
PDF detection heuristic — %PDF magic bytes, application/pdf content-type, or the base64 'JVBER' marker
Diagnostic-only function: it exists to answer 'which endpoint works' for an undocumented partner API, not to serve product traffic
Mode-aware Bonzah credential verification — test short-circuits to the shared platform creds, live actually authenticates
Why creds are trimmed before the test-mode short-circuit — a space-prefixed pasted password would be persisted unverified and then fail every live auth
tenants.bonzah_mode read from the DB is the source of truth for which API to verify against — the caller cannot pass a mode
Bonzah policy detail fetch for an already-issued policy (servicing path)
Per-tenant Bonzah credential + API-URL + token resolution shared by every Bonzah function
Excess-mileage charge calculation and idempotent ledger posting after return mileage is recorded
Pro-rata-by-day allowance MUST match the UI util — the old ceil-per-tier maths gave 1mo+1day two months of miles, so the server charged against a different allowance than the operator saw
An is_unlimited_mileage upgrade short-circuits the calculation and deletes any stale charge from a prior run
Rental-level mileage and excess-rate overrides beat the vehicle's values, and the override is stamped into the ledger reference
Idempotency by delete-then-recreate: every exit path first deletes the existing Excess Mileage charge, so re-recording mileage never stacks charges
Pickup and return odometer readings come from the giving/receiving rental_key_handovers rows, not from the rental
calculateTotalMileageAllowance() UI util — byte-duplicated in portal and booking and named as the parity target by the edge function
Record-anchored Stripe platform routing (UK/UAE) — resolve keys and connected account from the record that created the Stripe object, never the tenant's current payment_model
Booking rejection — release the pre-auth and unwind rental, vehicle and unpaid charges
Failures return HTTP 200 with success:false so supabase-js does not swallow the body as a FunctionsHttpError
payment_intent_unexpected_state and resource_missing are treated as already-released; the DB unwind proceeds regardless of what Stripe says
Gotcha: the catch block dereferences Stripe.errors.StripeError but Stripe is never imported in this file — the fallback path throws a ReferenceError
Admin rental cancellation orchestration — refund, insurance cancellation, ledger write-off, deposit-hold release, vehicle release
Release the deposit hold on ANY non-terminal status — the 7→11 deposit_hold_status widening (2026-08-10) stranded renters' authorised money on rentals cancelled mid-refresh
Rationale: reconcile-deposit-holds reconciles hold state against Stripe, it does NOT release holds for cancelled rentals — so nothing sweeps a missed release
Bonzah cancellation endorsement (/Bonzah/newendorse_cncl) per active policy, with the local status set to cancelled regardless of the API outcome
Unpaid Insurance ledger charges are written off (remaining_amount zeroed) so a cancelled rental stops carrying insurance debt
Refund path branches on live PaymentIntent status — requires_capture cancels the hold, succeeded creates a full/partial refund, anything else is skipped
The function sends no customer notification — it returns a notificationData payload for the portal caller to dispatch
The cancellation record is only ever logged and appended to rentals.notes — there is no cancellation audit table
Booking approval — capture the pre-auth and drive rental → Active / vehicle → Rented
Hard 409 overlap guard — refuse approval when another Pending/Active rental overlaps this vehicle's dates, returning the conflicting rental id
Buffer-time cooldown is advisory only — logged as a warning so an admin may deliberately override it, unlike the overlap check
'already been captured' is treated as success — retrieve the PaymentIntent and carry on so a retried approval still completes the DB transitions
Ledger settlement is delegated to apply-payment and its failure is logged, never fatal — Stripe has already taken the money
Partial deposit capture with remainder preservation
Stripe quirk: a partial capture RELEASES the uncaptured remainder — the product promise 'charge $1, keep $2 on hold' is why a rollover PI exists at all
Multicapture path keeps the remainder on the SAME PI (final_capture:false); pre-rollout holds and multicapture rejections fall back to a fresh rollover PI
Expired-hold self-heal — reconcile the DB to 'expired' and return code hold_expired at HTTP 200 so the UI can switch to Refresh-then-Charge instead of showing a raw non-2xx error
verify_jwt is satisfied by the PUBLIC anon key shipped in the booking bundle — why an explicit tenant guard runs before the rental fetch and before any Stripe call
The body's tenantId is a convenience hint for Stripe config only — it must never stand in for the rental's own tenant
Never re-hold the remainder on an auto-extend rental (renewal pricing replaces the deposit); manual extensions were re-allowed after the GMT incident, Jul 2026
ux_rental_charge_unique forces same-day deposit captures to merge into the existing Security Deposit charge rather than insert a second one
Captured deposit is recorded in-function as payment + Security Deposit charge + payment_application so Collected reflects the money received
Operator-initiated off-session charge of the card already on file for a rental

Scope limit: no stored-credential mandate exists yet, so damage/cleaning recovery (CA Civ. Code §1939.15(a), NY GBL §396-z(7) require permission captured AFTER the damage) is guarded only by dialog copy — 'copy is not a control'
Zero-decimal and three-decimal currency handling — refuse outright rather than risk charging 100x on an operator-typed amount
10-minute duplicate backstop behind the client idempotency key — the key stops a replay, this stops two genuinely distinct requests (two tabs, two operators) and needs explicit confirmDuplicate
charged_but_not_recorded — once money has moved the payments row is never rolled back and the charge is never silently refunded; the operator is told not to retry
Replay guard — an idempotent retry returns the same PaymentIntent, so an existing payments row for that PI short-circuits to alreadyRecorded instead of double-counting revenue
authentication_required gets its own error code so the UI offers 'email a payment link' rather than reporting an SCA challenge as a decline
Charge RBAC — super admin, head_admin or admin; a manager only when explicitly granted editor on the payments tab; viewers and ops are denied
validateStripeCustomerId runs first — a test-era customer id does not exist on the live Connect account (Kedic go-live incident: 12 blind retries because place-deposit-hold skips this check)
Settlement is apply-payment's job — calling the settle RPCs here as well would double-settle against portal callers that settle on the 'recorded' callback
Every attempt — succeeded, failed, requires_action, unrecorded — writes an audit_logs row carrying actor, card fingerprint fields and the duplicate override flag
A live charge with no connected account would land on the Drive247 platform balance instead of the operator's — refuse rather than misroute real money
placeDepositHoldAfter chains place-deposit-hold over service-role HTTP, deliberately writing no deposit_hold_* state here — that state machine is owned by place-deposit-hold
Trax AI create_reminder action with customer/vehicle entity resolution
Multiple entity matches return a clarification question as a plain string instead of an action proposal, so the AI never guesses which customer or vehicle was meant
AI-created reminders are stamped rule_code AI_<8 hex> so they are distinguishable from rule-engine reminders like BONZAH_LOW_BALANCE
A general reminder with no resolved entity falls back to object_id = tenantId, so object_type/object_id are never null
Trax AI action registry — OpenAI tool schemas filtered by portal role, each action carrying confirmationRequired and destructive flags
Two-method action contract: resolve() turns model params into a human-confirmable proposal (or a clarification string), execute() performs the write
Only create_reminder is registered — the AI-actions surface is one action wide despite the general framework
Trax AI — staff-facing RAG assistant (embedding + semantic search + live metrics + GPT)
Retrieval pipeline: generateEmbedding → match_documents → get_rag_metrics + get_pending_rental_requests → get_chat_history, all tenant-parameterised RPCs
Sentinel-block protocol — CHART_DATA and RENTAL_REQUESTS fences the prompt emits and the server strips out of the visible answer
Two-phase AI action flow — the model's tool call becomes a proposal, the client confirms, and execute_action re-checks RBAC server-side before writing
Every RAG input is tenant-scoped and the prompt explicitly forbids referencing or implying another tenant's data
The prompt declares the metrics JSON authoritative and forbids invented, estimated or rounded values — charts must copy the pre-built breakdown arrays verbatim
Explicit anti-trigger rules: greetings, thanks and 'how do I…' questions must never fire a tool; only a clear instruction to DO something may
Both turns are persisted to chat_messages with the retrieved sources and any chart payload attached to the assistant row
Blacklist identity matching — hard (exact phone/email/licence) versus soft (fuzzy name plus partial contact) verdicts
Soft match requires BOTH a Levenshtein ≤ 2 name and a partial contact overlap (last-7 phone digits or the email local-part), and is same-tenant only
Cross-tenant blacklist scan gated by tenants.cross_tenant_blacklist_enabled, with the origin tenant masked to null on a foreign hit
Gotcha: candidates are pulled with .limit(500) and no ordering, so matches beyond the cap are silently invisible — worst on the cross-tenant path
UK→UAE Stripe migration readiness gate — subscription track and own-Stripe track, each ready/warning/blocked with human-readable reasons
safeCount fails CLOSED — supabase-js RESOLVES with {error} and REJECTS on transport failure, so the old destructure turned every failed read into '0, nothing to block on'
Every non-terminal deposit_hold_status blocks the flip — a PaymentIntent cannot be moved between platform accounts, so a live hold would strand the renter's money
Platform filter applied in JS as 'not uae' rather than SQL '= uk' so a NULL or unrecognised anchor over-blocks instead of under-blocking
48h trial_end floor mirrors MIN_TRIAL_END_MS in create-uae-subscription-capture — inside that window UAE bills immediately and the tenant briefly pays both accounts
Saved cards are platform-scoped — active installment plans and auto-extend rentals charge a UK-minted customer/payment-method off-session and therefore hard-block the flip
Blocks unless the tenant's CURRENT stripe_mode has an OAuth-connected own account — the misroute guard that makes the flip impossible-to-green in the mode they actually charge in
The verdict live-verifies against Stripe (UK subscription, open invoices, Express balance) with the DB only as fallback; a failed live read degrades to a warning, never a crash
Unknown counts are surfaced to the UI as *Unknown flags so the admin screen can say 'unknown' rather than render a reassuring 0
Portal policy acceptance check/record against the tenant's current privacy and terms versions
Super admins skip DB logging entirely — their acceptance is frontend-only and never lands in policy_acceptances
Every lookup failure (unknown user, wrong tenant, unreadable tenant row, query error) resolves to needsAcceptance:true — the gate fails toward re-prompting
The caller is identified by a posted email rather than a JWT (verify_jwt = false), and acceptance also stamps tenants.policies_accepted_at
CORS/json/error helpers are re-declared inline instead of importing _shared/cors.ts, so this function drifts from the shared CORS contract
Recover a tenant's Connect account by scanning every connected account for metadata.tenant_id, then write the id and status back onto tenants
Full paginated scan of all connected accounts because Stripe cannot filter accounts by metadata — cost grows with every account on the platform
Uses the bare STRIPE_SECRET_KEY env at module scope — this function predates the dual test/live and UK/UAE client helpers and is blind to both

hyperedges.label: Deposit hold capture lifecycle: authorise the caller → detect a dead auth → capture (multicapture or rollover PI) → record the money as payment + charge + application → rewrite the hold state
Bonzah operator activation: training quiz graded server-side → partner reviews the submission → live-mode flip and credential verification → integration enabled → balance monitoring starts
UK→UAE platform migration safety net: record-anchored routing on every money path plus a fail-closed readiness gate that blocks on live holds, saved-card flows and unreadable counts
